newsitem.title: USA: Jesse Jackson rails against racism ahead of Oscars.
newsitem.headline: Jesse Jackson rails against racism ahead of Oscars.

text.p: Rev. Jesse Jackson railed against racism in Hollywood ahead of the entertainment industry's Oscars ceremony on Monday, a year after the civil rights activist picketed the annual event.

"Today there are still too few people of colour being hired as writers, directors, and producers," Jackson said. "It would seem the aspirations of blacks, Latinos and others have hit perpetual yield signs and in most cases have been held up at red lights throughout this lucrative industry."
Jackson also criticised TV programmes and movies with black casts such as the just-released "Booty Call" that he said exploited typically racist views and were written in "ebonics", or black English.

Speaking to reporters via a conference call from his Chicago headquarters, Jackson said he would not be demonstrating as he did during last year's ceremony but urged government agencies to take up his fight against discrimination in private industry.

Since organising last year's Oscar night demonstrations in several cities, Jackson said there had been only "moderate adjustment" in the entertainment industry's willingness to hire and nurture minorities.
Cuba Gooding Jr and Marianne Jean-Baptiste, nominated for best supporting actor and actress roles, were the only blacks nominated for major Academy Awards this year.
